synopsis: Independent assessment is distinct from engineering confidence: in most markets, the manufacturer's internal safety board and customers accept the evidence, while a four-month evidence decision concerns externally acceptable simulation credibility rather than engineering speed alone [f12288, f1455, f12290]. South African mining published its independent verification specification on 29 August 2025, and MOSH requires supplier verification plus independent physical verification at TRL4 and TRL7, including separate coverage where machine braking characteristics differ [f348, f2478, f2459, f5613]. This regime creates substantial scheduling risk: as of October 2025, laboratory lead time was 18 weeks and growing, throughput was 1.6 tests per week, and first-pass rates were 42%–83%, supporting immediate booking and provision for at least one retest [f5787, f5788, f5789, f5790]. A program starting in October 2026 could realistically have an assessor-seen credibility dossier by mid-2027; the proposed March–April 2027 readiness gate requires assessor feedback and an independent decision on readiness, restricted scope or fallback [f69, f10198]. Credible review requires claim-to-evidence traceability, a declared validity envelope, independent physical evidence and assessor-selected confirmation tests, with decisions constrained to demonstrated validity [f12200, f12291, f7887, f7603]. External acceptance precedents exist in road applications, but no independent performance test was found for the listed off-road automatic-braking vendors, no explicit acceptance of legacy field history as a simulator reference was found, and the EU Machinery Regulation assessor and competence requirements remain unidentified [f1260, f7566, f1242, f7948, f12294].
